HP:6000431.label: Elevated urinary glycolic acid level
HP:6000431.text: markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion

records.label: Proband
records.family: Arab consanguineous kindred with two brothers

phenotypes.text: markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion

quotes: Two brothers, born to consanguineous healthy parents of Arab descent, were evaluated for psychomotor delay associated with triple-A-like syndrome (anisocoria, alacrima and achalasia).

The proband showed markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion with normal excretion of oxalate, citrate and glycerate. Abdominal ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys with normal echotexture.
Direct DNA sequencing of glycolate oxidase gene (HAO1) revealed a homozygous c.814-1G>C mutation in the invariant -1 position of intron 5 splice acceptor site.

records.label: HAO1 knockout woman
quotes: The frameshift variant, rs1186715161 (present on a single Ensembl 99 transcript ENST00000378789.3:c.997delC, ENSP00000368066.3:p.Leu333SerfsTer4), for which the woman is homozygous, is predicted to truncate the final 37 amino acids of the HAO1 protein.

At genotype directed recall, her serum anion gap was normal, and plasma and urinary oxalate were both normal. However, confirming the loss of function predicted from the genetics, her plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate levels were markedly elevated (Table 1)

She declared British-Pakistani ethnicity. Renal ultrasound, carried out as part of a gynaecology assessment, was normal. She was overweight (BMI 30–35 kg/m2), and other than common non-serious short-term illnesses and pregnancy symptoms, otherwise healthy.

notes.statement: McGregor et al. (2020) exome sequenced 2 large population cohorts with a lot of autozygosity (Born in Bradford, Genes and Health). They identified a healthy British-Pakistani woman in her fifth decade who was homozygous for a frameshift in the HAO1 gene (c.997delC; p.Leu333SerfsTer4) that lies within a 5.2-Mb autozygous region. Her plasma glycolate was 12 times, and her urinary glycolate 6 times, the upper limit of normal, while her plasma and urinary oxalate were normal.
quotes: The volunteer was 7.4% autozygous at the DNA level and the genotype was within a long (5.2 Mb) autozygous region.
Her plasma glycolate levels were 12 times, and urinary glycolate 6 times, the upper limit of normal observed in healthy reference individuals (n = 67).

notes.statement: McGregor et al. (2020) expressed the p.Leu333SerfsTer4 HAO1 variant in CHO-K1 cells. It gave markedly reduced HAO1 protein, while mRNA levels were unaffected, and the protein was spread diffusely through the cells. This was consistent with loss of the C-terminal SKI peroxisomal targeting tripeptide.
quotes: Results with p.Leu333SerfsTer4 revealed markedly reduced HAO1 protein (mRNA levels were unaffected) with the p.Leu333SerfsTer4 HAO1 protein also diffusely distributed (mis-localised) within cells.
HAO1 protein is normally found exclusively in hepatocyte peroxisomes and requires the C-terminal tripeptide SKI for this targeting (Recalcati et al., 2001).

notes.statement: McGregor et al. (2020) ran plasma metabolomics and lipidomics (1,871 biochemicals) on the HAO1-null woman. Most of her metabolites were similar to those of 25 controls, but 18 biochemicals, including glycolate, were extreme outliers (more than 5 SD above controls). Unconjugated bile acids were raised and glycine- and taurine-conjugated bile acids were reduced, which the authors suggested might reflect reduced local glycine availability.
quotes: We observed that 18 biochemicals (including glycolate) were markedly elevated (extreme outliers at >5 sd compared to controls) in addition to other more modestly elevated biochemicals
The elevated cholic acid related compounds might be due to reduced local availability of glycine (a product of the glycolate pathway) to conjugate cholic acid and its bile acid derivatives

notes.statement: McGregor et al. (2020) compared the woman with healthy volunteers given lumasiran, an RNAi therapeutic targeting HAO1 for primary hyperoxaluria type 1. Her plasma and urinary glycolate were 3 to 5 times higher than the volunteers' peak levels at the highest dose. The authors estimated that she retains less than 2% residual glycolate oxidase activity, and concluded that lifelong HAO1 knockout was safe in her, supporting the safety of chronic HAO1 inhibition.
quotes: In healthy volunteers at the highest dose tested (6 mg/Kg) maximal plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate concentrations were 3–5 times less than observed in the HAO1 knockout woman.
Consequently, we estimate that this woman likely retains <2% residual glycolate oxidase activity.
In this woman, lifelong HAO1 knockout is safe and without clinical phenotype, de-risking a therapeutic approach and informing therapeutic mechanisms.

notes.statement: McGregor et al. (2020) found no homozygous predicted loss-of-function HAO1 variants among 141,456 individuals in gnomAD v2.1, where about 1 in 2,700 individuals is heterozygous. They estimated the expected frequency of homozygotes in an outbred population at about 1 in 30 million.
quotes: No complete knockout (homozygous predicted loss of function, pLOF) variants in HAO1 were observed in the online gnomAD v2.1 database of 141,456 whole exome/genome sequenced individuals
The cumulative frequency of known pLOF variants in HAO1 is low, in gnomAD v2.1 approximately 1 in 2700 individuals is heterozygous.
since the expected homozygote frequency in an outbred population would be only ~1 in 30 million individuals

notes.statement: Frishberg et al. (2014) used an in vitro hybrid-minigene approach, because HAO1 is liver-specific, to show that the c.814-1G>C mutation in the intron 5 splice acceptor site resulted in an abnormal splice variant in transfected cells.
quotes: Since HAO1 is a liver-specific enzyme, the effect of this novel mutation on splicing was validated by an in vitro hybrid-minigene approach. We confirmed the appearance of an abnormal splice variant in cells transfected with mutant minigene vector.

notes.statement: Frishberg et al. (2014) concluded that defective glycolate oxidase splicing caused isolated asymptomatic glycolic aciduria; the triple-A-like syndrome in the kindred was found to be unrelated to the metabolic abnormality.
quotes: Our results pinpoint the expression of defective splice variant of glycolate oxidase as the cause of isolated asymptomatic glycolic aciduria.
The genetic nature of triple-A-like syndrome in this kindred was found to be unrelated to this metabolic abnormality.

notes.statement: Frishberg et al. (2014) suggested that their observation supports substrate reduction (inhibition of glycolate oxidase) as a novel approach to treatment of primary hyperoxaluria type I.
quotes: This observation contributes to the development of novel approaches, namely, substrate reduction, for the treatment of primary hyperoxaluria type I.
